title: Which of the following techniques and/or circumstances DECREASES the risk or likelihood of causing TMJ injuries when performing mandibular extractions?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Final Exam: Inadequate support of the mandible
omfs: Application of excessive forces during the extraction
final: Previous history of TMJ issues
column5: Having the patient bite down on a bite block while the operator or an assistant pushes up on the anterior inferior border of the mandible.
column6: Using a 3-corner flap rather than an envelope flap.

title: A tooth may accidentally be displaced into the infratemporal fossa during extraction of a maxillary third molar. Which of the following statements regarding treatment is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Final Exam: If the tooth is visible at the time of displacement, it should be grasped and removed.
omfs: If the tooth is not visible at the time of displacement, no more than five blind attempts should be made to grasp it and remove it.
final: If the tooth cannot be immediately removed at the time of displacement, the site should be sutured, antibiotics should be prescribed, and the patient should be informed of the need for future removal of the tooth.
column5: If the tooth cannot be immediately removed at the time of displacement, removal should be delayed, allowing fibrosis to occur and stabilize the tooth, avoiding further displacement.
column6: Delayed removal of the displaced tooth is generally beyond the scope and capabilities of a general dentist and should be referred to an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon.

title: Which of the following statements about post-operative hemorrhage following an extraction is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Final Exam: It often occurs due to a patient's failure to properly follow instructions.
omfs: It may occur due to a “liver clot” which is a blood clot that forms outside of the extraction socket.
final: Injecting local anesthesia with epinephrine into the surgical site may help achieve hemostasis but it may also mask bleeding which could resume when the epinephrine effects wear off.
column5: It is always related to local factors and not a result of systemic medical issues or medications that the patient may be taking.
column6: Biting on a teabag may help slow or stop bleeding.

title: Which of the following instructions are NOT included in “sinus precautions” given to a patient when a maxillary posterior extraction may have resulted in an oro-antral communication?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Final Exam: Do not blow your nose for two weeks.
omfs: Sneeze with your mouth open.
final: Do not do any heavy lifting.
column5: Do not bend over.
column6: All of these instructions are included in “sinus precautions”.

title: Which of the following statements relating to maintaining hemostasis following oral surgical procedures is a TRUE statement that should be included in the instructions given to the patient?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Final Exam: The purpose of the patient biting on gauze after a procedure is to soak up the blood coming from the surgical site.
omfs: Bleeding can start and stop after a procedure and often is heavier after the numbing wears off.
final: It is extremely unusual for some bleeding to persist throughout the first 24 hours
column5: The longer the blood clot is kept in the extraction site, the greater the likelihood of developing a painful condition known as a DRY SOCKET.
column6: Patients can rinse, spit, smoke, use a straw, or do heavy lifting beginning one hour after an extraction.

title: Which of the following techniques is NOT a primary treatment modality for jaw tumors?

column6: None of these techniques can be primary treatment modalities for jaw tumors.

title: Which of the following statements about reconstruction following resection of jaw tumors is FALSE?

final: If reconstruction is delayed, it is not necessary to maintain the proper anatomical position of mandibular segments.

column6: Maintaining the inferior border of the mandible, if possible, aids in reconstruction.

title: Which of the following statements about marsupialization is TRUE?

omfs: Marsupialization inconveniences patients as they are required to irrigate the site once per week.
final: Tissue cannot be obtained for pathologic diagnosis when marsupialization is performed.
column5: Marsupialization is a definitive treatment after which no additional treatment is necessary.
column6: The risk of mandible fracture related to a large mandibular lesion is reduced immediately following the marsupialization procedure.

title: Which of the following statements about marsupialization is FALSE?

final: This technique may be helpful to allow eruption of a tooth that has been displaced by a cystic lesion.

column6: This lesion may be helpful to lessen the risk of fracture when removing a large cyst of the posterior mandible.

title: Which of the following statements related to biopsy procedures is FALSE?

title: Which of the following statements about flap design and development for the removal of impacted third molars is TRUE?

title: Which of the following statements pertaining to the removal of impacted teeth is TRUE?

column6: Insufficient bone removal and/or sectioning may complicate an extraction as the use of increased force may then become necessary.

title: Which of the following statements about PERICORONITIS related to a mandibular third molar is FALSE?
